title: Committee of Supply − Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: Budget caps downward adjustment
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced a permanent 2% downward adjustment to budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State from FY2017 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: During the Budget Statement speech, the Minister for Finance announced that a permanent 2% downward adjustment to the budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State will apply from financial year (FY) 2017 onwards.

sections.label: IRAS tax collection cost
sections.summary: IRAS's cost of tax collection and rates of arrears are among the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The cost of tax collection by IRAS is among the lowest in the world, and among the lowest rates of arrears as well.

sections.label: Gov-PACT scheme for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government will launch Gov-PACT, letting SMEs leverage Government-led demand to offer innovative solutions and strengthen capabilities and track record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Many jurisdictions have already practised this approach and we should move on this as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I was, hence, delighted to hear at this year's Ministry of Trade and Industry's (MTI's) COS that the Government will launch a new scheme known as the Government's enhanced Partnerships for Capability Transformation (Gov-PACT) where SMEs can leverage Government-led demand to participate and offer innovative solutions, in the process, strengthening their new capabilities and track record.

sections.label: Digitalisation master plan across agencies
sections.summary: A question asks whether a master plan exists for digitalisation and innovative technology across Government agencies with clear targets and KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Is there a master plan for the deployment of digitalisation and innovative technology across Government agencies, with clear targets and key performance indicators (KPIs)?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government should really adopt a whole-of-Government approach in data collection and leverage technology to improve efficiency and service delivery by eliminating the need for citizens to provide the same data repeatedly.

sections.label: UK Office for Budgetary Responsibility
sections.summary: The UK Office for Budgetary Responsibility, established in 2010, has five missions including five-year forecasts and judging fiscal target performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The United Kingdom (UK) Office for Budgetary Responsibility was established in 2010, and its missions are: one, to produce detailed five-year forecasts for the economy and public finances; two, judge the Government's performance against its fiscal targets; three, assess long-term fiscal sustainability; four, evaluate fiscal risks; and five, scrutinise the Government's costing measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The independent analysis of such an office can also provide input to the Elected President on whether or not to veto Supply Bills, should the Government wish to draw on Reserves not accumulated by the current Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that this is one of the most important decisions the President might have to make, there should be a non-partisan, professional and specialised outfit putting out independent assessments to assist the Elected President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He said, and I quote, "We will have to raise revenues through new taxes or raise tax rates" to keep our finances sustainable.

sections.label: Speculation on raising GST
sections.summary: There has been widespread speculation that the Government is looking to raise the Goods and Services Tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And what are the principles guiding these considerations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There has been widespread speculation that the Government is looking to raise the Goods and Services Tax (GST), with experts and journalists suggesting that it is no longer a matter of whether the Government will do it; it is simply a matter of when.

sections.label: GIRO tax deductions during unemployment
sections.summary: Workers on GIRO face ongoing tax deductions while unemployed, monthly or lump sum, with late payment penalties if unpaid.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Workers who have signed on to the General Interbank Recurring Order (GIRO) payments will experience ongoing tax deductions even during the period of unemployment, either monthly, or in a lump sum, and if they are unable to pay up, they are slapped with a late payment penalty.

sections.label: Tax competition and Singapore rates
sections.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing said tax competition is a major concern for Singapore and largely determines corporate and personal income tax rates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Minister Chan Chun Sing mentioned in his speech on Wednesday during the Budget debate last week, tax competition is a major concern for Singapore, and it determines to a large extent our policy on corporate and personal income tax rates.

sections.label: US tax moves and repercussions
sections.summary: Any US move to improve tax competitiveness will refresh its investor attractiveness and have major repercussions on its competitors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By virtue of its size, the relative strength of the US economy and its value as a consumer market, any move by the new US administration to improve its tax competitiveness will refresh its attractiveness to investors and have major repercussions on its competitors.

sections.label: FDI challenges and TPP setback
sections.summary: This will affect Singapore's ability to attract FDIs, especially given the TPP abandonment and other global challenges.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will affect our ability to attract FDIs in future.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These challenges are of particular concern in the current context, in light of the setback from the abandonment of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) and other global challenges.

sections.label: SMEs, GovTech research partnerships, procurement
sections.summary: SMEs with niche technologies could partner GovTech or agencies, but under 5% secure Government projects; a procurement fair was held.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could SMEs which have niche technologies relevant to the work be engaged through research partnerships with the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) or other agencies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, due to their large numbers and variety, it is estimated that less than 5% of our SMEs secure Government projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last year, the first Government procurement fair was held, in part, to encourage SMEs to participate in the Government procurement process.

sections.label: SME share of Government contracts
sections.summary: SMEs were reported winning over 60% of total Government contract value and about 85% of all Government tenders over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Last year, it was reported that SMEs were winning more than 60% of total Government contract value and about 85% of all Government tenders over the last three years.

sections.label: Set-aside for SME tenders
sections.summary: Urges Government to set aside at least 60% of total contract values for SMEs and award one-third of tenders to smaller SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As SMEs have clearly proven capable of handling Government tenders and projects, I urge the Government to set aside at least 60% of total Government contract values for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: In addition, award one-third of all Government tenders —

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: — to smaller SMEs with a turnover of less than $10 million.

sections.label: Incumbency advantage from awarded contracts
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry ensures awarded contracts do not later create an incumbency advantage for the awardee from the implemented project solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Further, how does the Ministry ensure that contracts awarded do not subsequently create an incumbency advantage for the awardee arising from the project solution implemented?

sections.label: Fair contract clauses for service buyers
sections.summary: Proposes fair contract validity, termination and non-punitive liquidated damages clauses to create transparency, a level playing field and gain-sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, a fair clause for a contract validity period to allow for prices to be agreed upon and also allow for price variations, including that for option years should there be any unforeseen changes in Government policy, for example, mandatory adoption of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and announcement of National Wages Council (NWC) guidelines during this period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, a termination clause that allows for reasonable engagement by both parties to address any issues, as well as enable both sides to give notice for early termination based on the agreed terms and conditions should issues remain unresolved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, liquidated damages should not be punitive but used as a professional tool to reasonably compensate service buyers for non-compliance of service standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In current practice, service buyers often dictate liquidated damages for service lapses and this is often blown out of proportion or used as a "cost-saving" measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With greater transparency in contractual obligations, it can create a level playing field for all businesses and encourage better gain-sharing practices that will benefit workers when the worries of unnecessary costs are alleviated with fair contracts and best practices.

sections.label: Annual value means-testing criterion
sections.summary: States that annual value of the home a person lives in is a key assessment criterion in means-testing programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One of the key assessment criteria in our means-testing programmes − and I accept and acknowledge that there is a whole range of these programmes − is the annual value of a home in which they live in, not own, but live in.

sections.label: Government transfers to HDB dwellers
sections.summary: Cites a Department of Statistics publication finding HDB dwellers received about four times the Government transfers of private estate dwellers in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In a publication by the Department of Statistics titled "Key Household Income Trends 2016", HDB dwellers, on average, received about four times the amount of Government transfers when compared to private estate dwellers in the same year in 2016.

sections.label: Lowest-income households in private property
sections.summary: Cites the same 2016 report finding 6.5% of households in the lowest 10% of monthly income live in private properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The same report by the Department of Statistics in 2016 found that 6.5% of households in the lowest 10% of monthly household income live in private properties.

sections.label: Annual value threshold $13,000
sections.summary: The annual value threshold of $13,000 has been fixed for at least the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Third, the annual value of $13,000 has been fixed as a threshold for the last five years at least, as far as I could tell.

sections.label: $13,000 annual value eligibility
sections.summary: At $13,000 annual value, only 1- or 2-room HDB flats would qualify based on 2016 fourth quarter median rental statistics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Thirteen thousand dollars in annual value means that any property which can fetch a market rent of about $1,100 per month would not qualify based on the latest 2016 fourth quarter median rental statistics, only 1- or 2-room HDB flats would then qualify.

sections.label: Means-testing and household needs
sections.summary: Means-testing criteria based on assessable income and annual value do not respond well to differing household needs and sudden events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What could be a decent household income for a family of three or four could be very different for a multigenerational household with elderly parents and in-laws in need of medical care and, at the same time, young children in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We really have to look beyond just one measure of assessable income and annual value and consider other factors as well and also consider dependants who rely on that household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some of these cases could well be long-term chronic ones, but there are others which could be short term caused by sudden catastrophic events like the loss of a key family breadwinner or the loss of a job, or a sudden acute need for medical care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All of these are likely scenarios, but our means-testing criteria just do not respond well to any of these happening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Consequently, there are families which, because of no or insufficient assistance rendered at the right time, fall into cracks and into acute difficulty.

sections.label: CHAS income eligibility
sections.summary: To be eligible for CHAS, an applicant's household monthly income per person must be $1,800 or below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, to be eligible for CHAS, an applicant's household monthly income per person must be $1,800 or below.

sections.label: Social transfer expenditure growth
sections.summary: Over the last 20 years, social transfer expenditures have on average grown about three times the rate of total expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: On average, over the last 20 years, social transfer expenditures have been growing about three times the rate of growth in total expenditures.

sections.label: Budget 2017 social transfers
sections.summary: Budget 2017 includes $4 billion in social transfers, half a billion in Special Transfers to households and $2.1 billion to businesses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: According to the detailed proposal for Budget 2017, on top of the $4 billion worth of social transfers, Special Transfers to Singaporean households will cost half a billion dollars, while Special Transfers to businesses, which include Workfare, will cost $2.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: For example, the one-off Special Payment will reach more than 1.3 million Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: Both the U-Save rebates and the S&CC rebates reach about 880,000 HDB households.

sections.label: Productivity growth measurement clarification
sections.summary: Productivity growth from 2009 to 2016 was 2.1% per annum by value-added per worker and 2.6% per annum by value-added per hour worked.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to just clarify that he was, in fact, referring to the period from 2009, which was the year the Economic Strategies Committee (ESC) based its recommendations, to 2016, and productivity growth in that period, as measured by value-added per worker, was 2.1% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we look at real value-added (VA) per actual hour worked, in other words, VA per hour, not VA per worker, so VA per hour, which is internationally viewed as a better measure of labour productivity growth, was 2.6% per annum over the same period.

sections.label: Online Government transactions share
sections.summary: As of 2015, nearly 90% of the most frequently used Government transactions could be conducted online, up from 76% in 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As of 2015, nearly 90% of the most frequently used Government transactions can be conducted online.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is a significant increase from 76% in 2013.

sections.label: Digital services by 2018
sections.summary: By 2018, citizens can look forward to this convenience for more than 150 Government digital services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By 2018, citizens can look forward to this convenience for more than 150 Government digital services.

sections.label: Business satisfaction with digital services
sections.summary: In the same survey done last year, 65% of businesses were satisfied with the Government's digital services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the same survey that we did last year, we found that 65% of businesses were satisfied with the Government's digital services.

sections.label: Portal grants and upcoming additions
sections.summary: The portal now offers six grants, including SPRING's Capability Development Grant, with four more grants expected by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The portal now offers six grants, including SPRING's Capability Development Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By the end of this year, businesses can look forward to four more grants, including the Building and Construction Authority's (BCA's) Mechanisation Credits and the National Park Board's (NPark's) Landscape Productivity Grant.

sections.label: Licences on LicenceOne
sections.summary: Currently over 80 licences from 16 agencies are on LicenceOne, and by FY2017 more than 100 licences will be available.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Currently, there are over 80 licences from 16 agencies on LicenceOne and, by FY2017, more than 100 licences will be available.

sections.label: SMEs share of Government contracts
sections.summary: Each year over 80% of Government contracts, about half of total contract value, go to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Each year, over 80% of Government contracts, comprising about half of total Government contract value, go to SMEs.

sections.label: Contracts won by smaller companies
sections.summary: By number of contracts, over 40% went to companies with revenues under $10 million, and almost half of these to micro-enterprises under $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By the number of contracts, more than 40% were won by companies with revenues of less than $10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And of these contracts, almost half were won by micro-enterprises with revenues of less than $1 million.

sections.label: Small-value Government tenders
sections.summary: About 90% of contracts called each year are below $100,000 in value, with more than 30,000 such contracts in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the same time, Government agencies are interested in ensuring that tenders are not too large that only a very small number of suppliers can tender for the project.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why, even today, a very high proportion of about 90% of contracts called by Government agencies each year are below $100,000 in value.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There were more than 30,000 of such contracts in 2016.

sections.label: Funding support for approved SMEs
sections.summary: Under the scheme, SMEs and startups with approved projects are eligible for up to 70% funding support for qualifying development costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, SMEs and startups whose projects are approved are eligible for up to 70% funding support for the qualifying development costs.

sections.label: Accredited companies winning contracts
sections.summary: Seventeen companies were accredited, 13 won contracts, and $60 million of Government pipeline opportunities have been generated to date.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Seventeen of these companies have been accredited, out of which, 13 have won contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We expect more to do so over time and they will benefit from the $60 million of Government pipeline opportunities that have been generated to date.

sections.label: Young company winning Government projects
sections.summary: The company was founded in 2013, accredited in May 2016, and then won six Government projects while still young without a significant track record.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The company was founded in 2013 and received accreditation in May 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It subsequently went on to win six Government projects when they were still a young company without a significant track record.

sections.label: GeBIZ Mall orders
sections.summary: An average of 5,000 orders worth $3.5 million yearly were placed through GeBIZ Mall over five years, with greater participation intended.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, an average of 5,000 orders per year have been placed through GeBIZ Mall.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This amounts to a value of $3.5 million per year and we intend to encourage greater participation on this platform.

sections.label: Company AGM and seal requirements
sections.summary: Requirements will be simplified: private companies meeting conditions are exempt from AGMs, and common seal use is removed for companies and LLPs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will simplify these requirements to give greater clarity to companies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will exempt all private companies from holding AGMs, provided they meet certain conditions, and we will also remove the requirement for companies and limited liability partnerships to use the common seals.

sections.label: Revised checklist criteria
sections.summary: The checklist was revised to cut criteria by about 50%, saving each trader around 14 man-hours of application time.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The checklist was revised to reduce the number of criteria by about 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, with the revised criteria, each trader can save around 14 man-hours of application time.

sections.label: Simplified corporate tax return
sections.summary: IRAS extended the simplified corporate tax return to companies with annual revenues under $5 million instead of $1 million, helping 28,000 more companies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: IRAS has extended tax filing using a simplified corporate tax return to companies with annual revenues of less than $5 million, instead of $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will help an additional 28,000 companies ease their tax filing compliance.

sections.label: Sustainable programme revenue options
sections.summary: Programmes must be sustainable long term, so all options are being studied to raise revenues for future expenditure needs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Any programme we put in place must be sustainable for the long term.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why we are studying all options carefully to determine the best way to raise revenues to support our future expenditure needs.

sections.label: Corporate income tax competitiveness
sections.summary: The 17% corporate income tax rate remains internationally competitive, and trends will be monitored to keep the tax system competitive and pro-growth.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At 17%, our corporate income tax rate is still competitive internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we will continue to monitor the trends and ensure that our tax system remains competitive and pro-growth.

sections.label: Progressive GST and vouchers
sections.summary: Higher-income households contribute more taxes while lower-income households receive more benefits, with GST Vouchers making the system progressive.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is a system where the higher-income households contribute more of the taxes and the lower-income households receive more of the benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And this is also why we have designed our GST system with a permanent scheme of GST Vouchers so that the overall system is progressive, with the rich paying more.

sections.label: OECD budget offices and Singapore finances
sections.summary: Other OECD countries set up budget offices after the global financial crisis, but Singapore has sound finances and balanced budgets, funding the Pioneer Generation Package with $8 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Likewise, a number of other Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries have set up budget offices or fiscal councils in the aftermath of the global financial crisis as the surge of government deficits and debts" left countries worried that fiscal rules were insufficient and "governments wanted to boost the credibility of their financial promises" to financial markets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: That is not the case here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our Government has a strong track record of sound finances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While many other countries are in a net debt position, we have consistently spent within our means and achieved a balanced Budget in each successive term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: A good example is the Pioneer Generation Package, announced in Budget 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We set aside $8 billion from Current Reserves to help fund this.

sections.label: Leaders promoted or recruited
sections.summary: Examples of leaders promoted within organisations include Chua Sock Koong and Goh Choon Phong, while others like Tan Chong Meng, Piyush Gupta and Neil McGregor were recruited from other companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: If you take a sampling, for example, we have seen leaders who are promoted from within organisations, such as Singapore Telecommunications' (Singtel's) Group CEO, Ms Chua Sock Koong, who first joined Singtel in 1989, and then we have Singapore Airlines' (SIA's) CEO, Mr Goh Choon Phong, who joined SIA in 1990.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: There are leaders who are recruited from other companies, like Mr Tan Chong Meng, who was with Shell before joining the Port of Singapore Authority (PSA), and Mr Piyush Gupta who held various senior management roles at Citigroup before joining DBS Group as CEO, and Mr Neil McGregor who will succeed Mr Tang Kin Fei as Sembcorp Group President and CEO with effect from April 2017.

sections.label: Schemes not income-dependent
sections.summary: Eligibility for SkillsFuture Credit, the Pioneer Generation Package and the Marriage and Parenthood Package is not dependent on income or wealth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, eligibility for the SkillsFuture Credit, the Pioneer Generation Package and the Marriage and Parenthood Package is not dependent on income or wealth.

sections.label: Silver Support and safety nets
sections.summary: The Silver Support Scheme is only for seniors with low lifetime income and little family support, as are ComCare and MediFund safety nets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: By the way, the Silver Support Scheme is not for all HDB dwellers, but only for seniors who have had low income through life and now have little family support; likewise, ComCare and MediFund as safety nets for those in need.

sections.label: Progressive social support system
sections.summary: All social schemes together form a progressive system where support is extended to all, but those with greater need receive more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: If we put together all our different social schemes, we have a progressive social system where support is extended to all, but those with greater need receive more.

sections.label: Annual value thresholds for schemes
sections.summary: Schemes use AV thresholds of $13,000 and $21,000, so only private properties in the top 20% are excluded.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: When property is taken into consideration, many schemes consider the AV with a threshold of $13,000 and/or $21,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: An AV threshold of $13,000 already covers all HDB flats, while the AV threshold of $21,000 covers about 80% of residential properties, including some lower-value private properties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This means only those who live in private properties with AVs in the top 20% are excluded.

sections.label: Government partnership with community
sections.summary: The Government will work in partnership with community organisations, businesses, unions and citizens within a system of checks and balances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As the Finance Minister has stressed in his Budget speech, we will need to work in partnership with community organisations and individuals, especially since many of our social challenges are complex and multi-dimensional.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: One key theme has recurred in these discussions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is about the role of Government in catalysing growth and building a strong and resilient society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will do this within a credible and trustworthy system of checks and balances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have made good progress in these areas and we will continue to refine and improve.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are committed to work in partnership with our businesses, the unions and citizens in this journey.

sections.label: SingPass service sign-ups
sections.summary: All SingPass users can potentially access a service that automatically fills up information and forms with different Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: So, what would the Government do to get more sign-ups in this area?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, that will mean that all SingPass users can potentially access this service where, through one touch, you can automatically fill up information and forms with different Government agencies.

sections.label: Consent and data sharing outreach
sections.summary: Singaporeans must give consent for data sharing, and outreach and education efforts aim to raise take-up of the service over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Ultimately, Singaporeans must also give consent for their data to be shared for privacy reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There will be effort to reach out and educate people and to show them how useful the service is, what can it do for them, the convenience that it provides and, through that, we hope the take-up of the service will eventually start to go up over time.

sections.label: Preparing ahead, options open
sections.summary: The Government is preparing ahead and studying and keeping all options open at this time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The point is that we are preparing ahead and we are studying and keeping all options open at this time.

sections.label: GST with permanent voucher
sections.summary: GST is designed with a permanent voucher to make it a progressive consumption tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The way we have designed GST with a permanent voucher is to make it a progressive consumption tax.

sections.label: Avoiding loss of market confidence
sections.summary: The approach is to ensure international markets do not lose confidence in us to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With regard to the first clarification on whether we should need to wait till international markets to lose confidence before setting up such an institution, I think the correct approach to take is to make sure that international markets do not lose confidence in us to begin with.

sections.label: AAA rating shows market confidence
sections.summary: We must never reach that situation, and markets already have confidence in us, shown by our AAA rating.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the short answer really to that clarification is that we must make sure that we never get to that situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are already in the situation where international markets have confidence in us, and that is indicated by our AAA rating.

sections.label: Elected President seeking expertise
sections.summary: The Elected President can seek expertise from consultants, not necessarily an OBR, and has access to the Council of Presidential Advisors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Elected President, of course, has access to the Council of Presidential Advisors, but he is not precluded from seeking expertise from consultants or any other sort of expertise that he may need in order to make the kind of decisions that he needs to make under the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it does not necessarily have to take the form of an OBR.
